coverage_note: Resumed an interrupted run: the 9 findings and 9 verified_correct entries about help / about / remote-access / pairing came from the first attempt and are kept verbatim. findings.title: Tutorial Tours run as a modal on whatever screen you are on and tell you to click tabs that are not there -- and the modal blocks every one of them
findings.what_happened: Settings > Help & Tutorials > Tutorial Tours > Equipment Setup > Start opens a centred modal dialog with a full-screen scrim, ON THE SETTINGS SCREEN. Step 1 reads 'Equipment Profiles -- Click the Profiles tab to manage your equipment configurations.' There is no Profiles tab on the Settings screen, and the scrim swallows clicks so the user cannot go find one: with the overlay up I clicked the left-nav 'Imaging' entry (root 240,350) and the app stayed on Settings with the overlay unchanged. All 4 steps behave the same way ('Click the Connections tab', 'Check the status indicators for each device') -- it is a slideshow of instructions about a screen you are not on and cannot navigate to.
findings.expected: Starting a tutorial should route to the screen the tutorial is about (Equipment) and spotlight the real control, or at minimum let the underlying UI stay clickable so the instruction can be followed. NINA/SGP tours anchor to the widget being described.
findings.repro: Fresh profile > skip onboarding > gear icon > Help & Tutorials > scroll to Tutorial Tours > Equipment Setup 'Start'. Observe the modal appears over Settings. Click left-nav Imaging: nothing happens.

findings.title: About page's GitHub and Documentation links are placeholders that 404 / do not resolve
findings.what_happened: Settings > About offers three link buttons: GitHub, Documentation, Discord. GitHub opens https://github.com/skotiq-astro, which returns HTTP 404 -- the real project repo is https://github.com/Scdouglas1999/Skotiq (HTTP 200, per the repo README badge). Documentation opens https://skotiq.astro/docs; 'skotiq.astro' does not resolve in DNS at all (.astro is not a delegated TLD). Discord opens https://discord.gg/skotiq, which is not a Skotiq invite. Clicking GitHub in the app produced no error banner -- the launch is reported as successful and the user is dropped on a 404.
findings.expected: The three community links a shipped app puts on its About page must point at the real destinations: github.com/Scdouglas1999/Skotiq, the docs (docs/index.md is what the README points at), and a real Discord invite -- or the button should not exist.
findings.repro: gear icon > Settings > About > click GitHub. Then: curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://github.com/skotiq-astro -> 404; getent hosts skotiq.astro -> no answer.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-15.png (the three buttons rendered). curl: github.com/skotiq-astro -> 404, github.com/Scdouglas1999/Skotiq -> 200, skotiq.astro -> DNS FAILS.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/about_settings.dart:102,109,116 (and the mobile duplicates at :102/:109/:116 vs desktop :128/:135/:142)
findings.proposed_fix: Hoist the three URLs into one const block and set them to the real repo/docs/invite; add a launch-failure path that surfaces the URL (the existing showErrorSnackBar only fires when canLaunchUrl is false, which is not the failure mode here).
findings.verdict_reasoning: Verified at source and over the network. about_settings.dart hard-codes the three URLs twice (mobile Wrap :102/:109/:116, desktop Row :128/:135/:142), exactly as cited. curl https://github.com/skotiq-astro -> 404; curl https://github.com/Scdouglas1999/Skotiq -> 200; getent hosts skotiq.astro -> no answer (.astro is not a delegated TLD, so Documentation can never resolve). The Discord claim is true but for a sharper reason than stated: discord.gg/skotiq 301s to discord.com/invite/skotiq and the Discord API returns a VALID invite to guild 1370106030754631690 'Skotiq Gaming Community' -- an unrelated gaming server, so the button works and drops the user in a stranger's Discord, which is worse than a dead link. _launchUrl only surfaces an error when canLaunchUrl/launchUrl returns false, which a 404 page never does, so 'no error banner' is correct by construction.

findings.title: Remote Access claims 'Localhost stays frictionless for this machine' -- localhost is not exempt from auth at all
findings.what_happened: With Enable Remote Access on, the page's footer note reads 'Localhost stays frictionless for this machine, while non-local clients must pair before they can control the app', the 'Open on this computer' card says 'Use this link from the same machine to confirm the dashboard is working before sharing it elsewhere', and Connection details reports Authentication = 'Paired devices required remotely'. All three say local is special. It is not: from 127.0.0.1, GET /api/status -> 401 {'error':'Authentication required','message':'Missing Authorization header or session cookie'}; so do /api/images/recent, /api/auth/csrf and POST /api/auth/cookie. The bytes returned to 127.0.0.1 and to 192.168.1.20 are identical 401s. Only the static /dashboard shell is 200, and it can load no data. The auth middleware has no loopback branch at all.
findings.expected: Either implement the documented loopback exemption (peer address is loopback -> full-scope identity), or change the copy so it does not promise a local escape hatch that does not exist. As written, an operator clicking 'Open Local Dashboard' to 'confirm the dashboard is working' sees a dead page and concludes the server is broken.
findings.repro: Settings > Remote Access > Enable Remote Access. Then: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/status -> 401. curl http://localhost:<port>/api/status -> 401. curl http://192.168.1.20:<port>/api/status -> 401.
findings.evidence: Live 401 bodies captured from 127.0.0.1:8080 and 127.0.0.1:8099 (both ports I ran on). /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-20.png shows the 'Open on this computer' copy, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-19.png shows Connection details.
findings.where: copy: packages/skotiq_app/lib/localization/skotiq_localizations/translations.dart:389 and :399; enforcement: apps/desktop/lib/headless_api_server/http_middleware.dart:758-770 (token==null -> 401, no peer-address check anywhere in the chain).
findings.proposed_fix: Add an explicit loopback grant in the auth middleware keyed on the shelf connectionInfo remote address (and NOT on any forwarded header), or drop the 'frictionless' sentence and relabel the card 'Open the dashboard (you will need to pair this browser)'.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Enabled remote access on port 8391 (ss shows 0.0.0.0:8391). From 127.0.0.1: /api/status -> 401 {'error':'Authentication required','message':'Missing Authorization header or session cookie'}; /api/images/recent -> 401; /api/auth/csrf -> 401; /api/system/info -> 401. Only GET /dashboard is 200 (static shell). All three copy strings are still live: the footer note, the 'Open on this computer / Use this link from the same machine to confirm the dashboard is working' card, and Connection details -> Authentication 'Paired devices required remotely' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-15.png). Locations check out: translations.dart:389 remoteAccessInfoBody and :398-399 remoteAccessLocalActionTitle/Body; http_middleware.dart has no peer-address branch anywhere in the auth chain (its only 'loopback' mentions concern the rate-limit trusted-proxy header and CORS) and the token==null -> 401 return at :759-771 fires regardless of peer.

findings.title: Paired devices live in ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db -- outside the app database, outside the configured data dir, and split across two stores
findings.what_happened: I launched a completely fresh scratch profile (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-system/data, --fresh, empty skotiq.db). Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing immediately listed 12 devices paired 6/15/2026 and 7/20/2026 -- the developer's real, months-old pairings. They are not in skotiq.db; PairingDatabase opens getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/pairing.db, i.e. ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db, which ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR entirely. Two such stores exist on this machine: ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db (12 active rows, mtime Aug 1) and ~/Skotiq/pairing.db (0 rows, mtime Jul 29) -- the same install has written to two different locations depending on how getApplicationDocumentsDirectory resolved.
findings.expected: Long-lived remote credentials belong in the app database (or at minimum under the configured data dir) so that (a) Backup & Restore captures them, (b) moving the data directory moves them, (c) they cannot silently fork into two stores. As shipped, restoring a backup on a new machine silently loses every pairing, and a launch context where XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR differs presents an empty device list with no error.
findings.repro: drive_linux.py start --profile <new> --fresh (scratch data dir) > Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing. Observe 12 devices. sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/<profile>/data/skotiq.db '.tables' -> no pairing tables. sqlite3 ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db 'select count(*) from paired_devices where is_active=1' -> 12, matching the UI exactly. ls ~/Skotiq/pairing.db -> a second, empty store.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-22.png (12 devices in a fresh profile). UI count 12 == DB is_active count 12. Device names/dates match row-for-row (Dashboard 2026-06-15, Android companion 2026-07-20 x3...).
findings.where: packages/skotiq_remote_protocol/lib/src/database/pairing_database.dart:401-410 (_openConnection -> getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/pairing.db)
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the pairing DB through the same directory resolver the main database uses (SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR-aware application-support dir), and migrate any existing Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db on first run. Include it in the backup manifest.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced from a --fresh scratch profile (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/v-settings-system/data). Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing immediately listed 13 devices paired 6/15/2026, 7/20 x3, 7/22, 7/25 x3, 7/26 -- months older than the profile. The scratch skotiq.db has NO pairing table; sqlite3 ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db 'select count(*) ... is_active=1' returns 13, matching the UI count exactly and the names row-for-row. (Finding said 12; it is 13 now because concurrent audit agents paired since -- the count tracking the shared store IS the defect.) Cited location is exact: pairing_database.dart:401-410 _openConnection uses getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/pairing.db with no data-dir override anywhere. Two-store claim holds: ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db (13 active, mtime Aug 1) and ~/Skotiq/pairing.db (0 rows, mtime Jul 29).

findings.title: After a device pairs successfully the desktop keeps showing the pairing code counting down, and the device list does not update
findings.what_happened: I pressed Start Pairing Mode, read the code ASTRO-NEBULA-1815 off the screen, and completed pairing over HTTP (POST /api/pairing/verify -> 200 with a bearer token). The server immediately invalidated the code (a second verify with the same code returned invalid_pairing_code) and wrote the 13th row into paired_devices. The desktop screen did not react at all: 30s later it still displayed 'Enter this code on your device: ASTRO-NEBULA-1815 / Expires in 04:18 / Cancel Pairing', and Paired Devices still listed 12 entries. Only after manually pressing the small refresh icon did the 13th device appear.
findings.expected: The instant a code is consumed the panel should close and announce which device paired -- that confirmation is the operator's only way to know the phone in their hand is the device that just connected. Showing a live countdown for a code the server has already destroyed is a false statement, and it invites the operator to read the dead code to a second device.
findings.repro: Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing > Start Pairing Mode. From a shell: curl -X POST -d '{"code":"<code>","deviceName":"x","deviceId":"x","deviceType":"browser"}' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/pairing/verify. Watch the desktop: unchanged. sqlite3 ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db 'select count(*) from paired_devices where is_active=1' -> 13 while the UI shows 12.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-23.png (code panel), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-24.png (still counting down at 04:03 after the pair completed). Tree: 12 'Paired:' rows vs DB 13. After pressing refresh: 13 rows, 'audit-probe ... Paired: 1m ago'.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/pairing_screen.dart:96/215 (loadPairedDevices is only called on init and on the manual refresh button; nothing subscribes to pairing completion).
findings.proposed_fix: Have the pairing session emit a completion event (the server already knows) and drive the panel from it: close the code card, toast '<deviceName> paired', and reload the list.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Manage Pairing > Start Pairing Mode; code NEBULA-MOON-4612. POST /api/pairing/verify -> 200 with a bearer token; a second verify with the same code -> 401 invalid_pairing_code, so the server destroyed it immediately, and paired_devices went 13 -> 14 active rows. The desktop did not react: at +5s and again at +60s the tree still read 'Enter this code on your device: / Expires in 04:35 ... 04:18 / Cancel Pairing', and the list rendered 13 'Paired:' rows against the DB's 14. Location is right: pairing_screen.dart:94-96 _initialize() is the constructor-time load, :215 loadPairedDevices, and the only other caller is the manual refresh IconButton at :484 -- nothing subscribes to pairing completion.

findings.title: Paired devices always say 'Not seen yet / No connection recorded yet' -- last_connected_at is never written
findings.what_happened: Every one of the 13 paired devices shows the badge 'Not seen yet' and the line 'No connection recorded yet'. I proved this is untrue for at least one of them: after pairing 'audit-probe' I made three authenticated GET /api/status calls with its bearer (200, 200, 200) and then opened an authenticated WebSocket to /events (HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols, held open 60s). paired_devices.last_connected_at for that device stayed NULL and the UI still says 'Not seen yet'. All 12 pre-existing devices -- including ones that demonstrably drove this app in earlier sessions ('ui-audit-avd', 'Lead Harness') -- are likewise NULL.
findings.expected: last_connected_at should be stamped whenever a device authenticates. Without it the operator cannot tell a phone that is still in use from a stale credential, which makes the revoke list unusable: 7 of the 13 rows are named 'Android companion' with identical subtitles and no last-seen, IP or model to tell them apart.
findings.repro: Pair a device via POST /api/pairing/verify, call GET /api/status with the returned bearer (200), then sqlite3 ~/Documents/Skotiq/pairing.db "select device_name,last_connected_at from paired_devices where device_id='audit-probe-rss'" -> last_connected_at empty. Settings > Remote Access > Manage Pairing > refresh: row still reads 'No connection recorded yet'.

findings.title: A profile saved without optics can never be edited again: Save is rejected because of the 0 the app itself stored, and the rejection is invisible on screen
findings.what_happened: New Profile writes focal_length=0.0 / aperture=0.0. Re-open that profile, press Edit, change ONLY the name, press Save: nothing happens. No banner, no field-level error, no colour change -- the button appears dead. I clicked Save five times over three minutes and the DB never changed (still 'Backup Test Rig' while the field read 'Local Work Do Not Lose'). The failure is real and has a message -- the accessibility tree at that moment contains 'Focal length must be a positive number (leave blank if unknown)' and 'Aperture must be a positive number (leave blank if unknown)' -- but a full-window screenshot taken between the click and that tree read shows no such text anywhere on screen (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-67.png), and neither does a full-resolution capture of the bottom 160px where the snackbar would sit (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-snack-1.png). The snackbar is rendered underneath the persistent bottom status bar. Clearing both optics fields let the save through -- and it stored 0.0 again, so the profile is right back in the unsavable state next time.
findings.expected: Blank optics must round-trip as blank/NULL, not as 0.0 that the validator then rejects; and a rejected save must show its reason where the user is looking (inline under the offending field, plus a visible banner). As shipped, the very first thing a user does after creating a profile -- open it and fill something in -- hits a dead Save button with no explanation.
findings.repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > New Profile > name 'X' > Create. Overflow menu > Edit > change the name > Save. Nothing happens; sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db 'select name,focal_length,aperture from equipment_profiles' still shows the old name and 0.0/0.0. Now clear Focal Length and Aperture and press Save: it saves, and stores 0.0/0.0 again.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-64.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-67.png (identical -- edit form with 'Local Work Do Not Lose' typed, Focal Length 0, Aperture 0, no error visible) taken immediately after the Save click; tree read after that same click contains the two validation strings; DB unchanged across all attempts.
findings.where: validator: ProfileValidator.parseOptional... (focal/aperture 'must be a positive number') reached from packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/equipment_profiles_screen_parts/profile_details.dart:175-200; the empty-field -> 0.0 write is in the same save path; the snackbar is shown by the settings scaffold underneath the app's bottom status bar.
findings.proposed_fix: Persist blank optics as NULL (the column is already nullable in the export -- focalLength shows as a number only when set), treat 0 as 'unset' on read, and render validation failures inline on the fields plus a banner above the status bar.
findings.verdict_reasoning: SYMPTOM CONFIRMED, HALF THE STATED CAUSE REFUTED. Confirmed: New Profile wrote id=1 focal_length=0.0 aperture=0.0; the Edit form pre-fills both optics fields with a literal '0'; changing only the name and pressing Save left the DB untouched across repeated attempts; clearing BOTH optics fields let the save through and stored 0.0/0.0 again, putting the profile straight back in the rejecting state. Code is exact: _parseOptic (equipment_profile_validation.dart) returns ok(0.0) for blank but fails any value <= 0 with 'must be a positive number (leave blank if unknown)', while the model stores blank as the 0 sentinel and the editor renders that sentinel as '0'. REFUTED: 'nothing happens, no banner, the button appears dead, a full-window screenshot shows no such text'. Burst capture (250 ms interval, numpy diff vs baseline) shows a full-width red SnackBar carrying both messages appearing ~0.5 s after the click and persisting for its 4 s duration. The earlier screenshot was taken inside the entrance-animation latency. The finding IS right that there is no field-level error and no colour change on the offending fields. Downgraded to P2: the user gets a visible banner naming the exact fix, so this is a round-trip trap, not silent failure.
findings.location_wrong: profile_details.dart:175-200 -- the optics validators are actually at :170 and :172, the error is raised at :219, and the whole _validateAndBuild is :167-248

findings.title: Backups are written to ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups regardless of the configured data directory, so bundles from different databases pile into one undifferentiated 'Recent Backups' list
findings.what_happened: I launched a brand-new scratch profile with SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-system/data and an empty skotiq.db. The backup directory is ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups and ignores the data-dir override entirely, so this sandboxed instance also *wrote* into it: skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-27-37, -27-44, -27-45 and -30-25 are snapshots of my throwaway database (the 10:30 one records profilesCount: 0, taken right after I deleted every profile) sitting in the same list as the real ones. Nothing in the row -- name, size, date, icon -- says which database a bundle came from. A user with two installs, or anyone who has ever moved their data directory, is one click away from restoring a foreign configuration over their live one. As with pairing.db there are also two directories on this machine (~/Documents/Skotiq/backups with 9 bundles and ~/Skotiq/backups with 4), i.e. the same install has written backups to two places.
findings.expected: Backups belong under the configured data directory, and each row should show what it contains (profiles/sequences/targets counts are already in the bundle metadata) and which install/machine wrote it. findings.repro: drive_linux.py start --profile <new> --fresh > Settings > Backup & Restore. The list is non-empty on a first-ever launch. ls ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups -> the same 8 files, plus new skotiq_autosave_* written by the sandbox. python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('.../skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-30-25.892145.nsbackup'))['metadata'])" -> profilesCount 0, i.e. my scratch DB.

findings.where: the backup service's directory resolution (getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups) rather than the SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR-aware resolver used by skotiq.db
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the backup directory through the same data-dir resolver as the main database; stamp an install id into the bundle and show bundle contents (profiles/sequences/targets) in each Recent Backups row.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on a first-ever launch. Settings > Backup & Restore came up with a NON-EMPTY list -- 9 bundles dated Aug 1/Aug 2 this profile never created -- and 'Last Full Backup Aug 2, 2026 12:03'. Merely opening the screen also WROTE into the shared dir: ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups gained autosaves at 12-03-46/47/48 whose metadata is my throwaway DB (settingsCount 121, profilesCount 0), listed alongside the developer's real bundles. A fourth file appeared at 12-03-53 with profilesCount 1 while my DB had zero profiles -- a CONCURRENT audit instance writing into the same list, i.e. the finding's two-installs scenario happening live. `find /tmp/ns-audit/v-settings-system -iname '*backup*'` returns nothing. Root cause pinned: backup_service.dart:1025-1030 _getBackupDirectory -> getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups; the _backupDirectoryProvider override (:121/:149) is referenced from exactly one place in the repo, backup_service_listing_test.dart:34, so production has no data-dir-aware path. Rows render name + size + date only, so nothing identifies the source database.

findings.title: Backup & Restore contradicts itself about what restore does -- one card says nothing is merged, the confirm dialog says nothing is deleted
findings.what_happened: The Backup & Sync card states: 'Sync is bundle-based: restoring replaces local configuration - nothing is merged.' The restore confirmation on the same screen states the opposite: 'This imports "<file>" without deleting your current data. Settings with the same keys may be updated, and library items from the backup may be added.' I measured which is true for the local path: I inserted app_settings key 'audit_canary'='present' (not in the bundle), deleted every equipment profile, then restored the bundle. Result: the profile came back AND audit_canary was still 'present' -- merge semantics. So the Backup & Sync sentence is the false one, and it is the more dangerous direction to be wrong in: a user who believes 'replaces local configuration' will restore expecting a clean slate and instead get a hybrid of two configurations with no way to tell which settings came from where.
findings.expected: One sentence, true for both the local and the remote path, and a restore that states exactly what it will do to each category (settings overwritten by key, library items added, nothing removed).
findings.repro: Settings > Backup & Restore. Read the Backup & Sync paragraph. Click the restore icon on any Recent Backups row and read the dialog. Then: sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db "insert into app_settings values('audit_canary','present')"; delete from equipment_profiles; restore the bundle; both the profile and audit_canary are present afterwards.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-58.png (the 'nothing is merged' paragraph) and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-60.png (the 'without deleting your current data' dialog). SQL before/after quoted above.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/backup_screen.dart (Backup & Sync description vs the restore confirm dialog copy)
findings.proposed_fix: Make the sync paragraph describe the actual merge semantics, or make the remote restore genuinely replace and say so in both places.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Both sentences are true of their own operation; the finding compared copy from two different restore paths. The 'Sync is bundle-based ... nothing is merged' paragraph belongs to CloudSyncCard (cloud_sync_settings.dart:377-378, rendered on the Backup screen via backup_screen.dart:485) and describes the WebDAV/S3 pull-and-restore, which really does replace -- cloud_sync_settings.dart:324 calls service.pullAndRestore(..., replaceExisting: true) and its own confirm dialog (:313-314) repeats the replace wording. The 'without deleting your current data' dialog is ConfirmDialog.restore (utils/confirm_dialog.dart:88-100), used by backup_screen.dart:236 for a LOCAL Recent-Backups restore, which calls backupService.restoreBackup(replaceExisting: false) at :265-268 -- merge semantics, exactly as the dialog says. The verifier's experiment (canary survives, profile returns) is the documented behaviour of the local path and does not show the sync sentence is false. A mild UX ambiguity remains -- two restore semantics on one screen -- but the reported defect does not hold.
findings.location_wrong: Cited packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/backup_screen.dart, which contains neither string. They live in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/cloud_sync_settings.dart:313-314,377-378 and packages/skotiq_app/lib/utils/confirm_dialog.dart:96-98.

findings.title: Restore silently drops a backed-up equipment profile when its row id is already taken, and still reports 'Restored 123 items'
findings.what_happened: The bundle skotiq_backup_2026-08-02T10-43-32.295333.nsbackup contains exactly one equipment profile: {"id": 3, "name": "Backup Test Rig"} (metadata: settingsCount 122, profilesCount 1 -> 123 items). Locally, row id 3 existed but had been renamed to 'Local Work Do Not Lose'. I restored that bundle. The toast said 'Restored 123 items. Restart Skotiq before the next run.' The DB afterwards: 3|Local Work Do Not Lose|1 -- one profile, the local one, unchanged. 'Backup Test Rig' was neither inserted nor applied over row 3; it was dropped on the floor. The same restore into a database where id 3 was free DID bring the profile back (I verified that first, after deleting every row), so the discriminator is the id collision, not the bundle. The count in the message is the bundle's item count, not the number of items actually applied, so it is a claim the app has not checked.
findings.expected: Restore must not key library items on the backup's row ids -- ids are local and get reused as soon as you delete the highest row. Re-key on content (name) or insert with a fresh id, and report what was actually written ('122 settings updated, 1 profile added, 0 skipped'), never the bundle's own count.
findings.repro: Create a profile, Create Backup, rename that profile (or delete it and create another that takes the same rowid), then restore the bundle from Recent Backups. Toast claims all items restored; sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db 'select id,name from equipment_profiles' shows the backed-up profile is absent.
findings.evidence: Bundle JSON equipmentProfiles[0] = id 3 / 'Backup Test Rig'; DB after restore = 3|Local Work Do Not Lose|1; tree after restore = 'panel: Restored 123 items. Restart Skotiq before the next run.' Control case: with equipment_profiles emptied, the same bundle restored the profile back as id 3.
findings.where: the restore path in the backup service (row-id-keyed upsert/ignore for equipmentProfiles) called from packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/backup_screen.dart
findings.proposed_fix: Strip ids on restore and insert as new rows (matching existing rows by name to update), and build the success message from the write result rather than from bundle metadata.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with my own bundle plus a control case. Bundle skotiq_backup_2026-08-02T12-13-00 contained equipmentProfiles[0] = {id:1,'VSS Renamed B'}, metadata settingsCount 122 + profilesCount 1 = 123. I renamed local row id 1 to 'VSS Local Keep' and restored: toast read verbatim 'Restored 123 items. Restart Skotiq before the next run.' while sqlite3 afterwards showed 1|VSS Local Keep -- the backed-up profile neither inserted nor applied. CONTROL: with equipment_profiles emptied, the SAME bundle restored it back as 1|VSS Renamed B, so the id collision is the discriminator. Mechanism confirmed in code: _importProfiles inserts with the backup's row id under InsertMode.insertOrIgnore and increments count unconditionally, so itemsRestored is rows ATTEMPTED, not rows written. One nuance in the app's favour that the finding omits: the confirm dialog hedges with 'library items from the backup may be added' -- but the toast then states a definite count it never checked. P1 retained.
findings.location_wrong: cited only as 'the restore path in the backup service ... called from backup_screen.dart'; the defect lines are sequence_codec.dart:50-52 (id taken from the bundle), :114 (InsertMode.insertOrIgnore) and :116 (unconditional count++), with backup_screen.dart:267 forcing replaceExisting:false and :275 printing the count

findings.title: Every Settings snackbar renders underneath the persistent bottom status bar, so all success and failure feedback in Settings is invisible
findings.what_happened: Four separate Settings actions produce a SnackBar that exists in the widget tree but never appears on screen, because the Settings scaffold's snackbar is drawn at the bottom of the body while the app's always-on status bar (Idle | profile | Camera Disconnected | ... | LST) is painted on top of it. Confirmed cases: (1) a rejected profile Save -- tree contains 'Focal length must be a positive number (leave blank if unknown)' while the full-window capture /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-67.png shows nothing; (2) a failed catalog download -- tree contains 'Download failed: Exception: Annotation catalog download failed' while a full-resolution capture of the bottom 200px at the same moment (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-75.png) shows only the status bar; (3) 'Failed to save profile: Exception: Profile not found'; (4) 'Restored 123 items. Restart Skotiq before the next run.' In every case I captured the screen between the click and a tree read that still contained the message, so the message was live and not yet dismissed. The user's experience is a button that does nothing, for both failures and successes.
findings.expected: Feedback must be visible. Either give the SnackBar a bottom margin equal to the status-bar height (Flutter: SnackBarBehavior.floating with margin), or host it above the status bar in the shell.
findings.repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > New Profile > Edit > rename > Save (rejected). Or Settings > Catalogs > Download Standard (~50 MB) (VizieR TAP currently 503). Take a screenshot immediately; nothing is shown. Then run drive_linux.py tree and find the message text in the accessibility tree.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-67.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-75.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-snack-1.png -- all captured while the corresponding message was present in the accessibility tree.
findings.where: the ScaffoldMessenger used by packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/* vs the persistent status bar in the desktop shell
findings.proposed_fix: Set SnackBarBehavior.floating with a bottom margin >= status-bar height for the settings scaffold, or route settings feedback through the shell's own notification surface.
findings.verdict_reasoning: The snackbars are visible; I measured rather than eyeballed. Method: xdotool click, then `import -window root` every 250-300 ms, then numpy pixel-diff each frame against a pre-click baseline. Case 1 (rejected profile Save): frames 1-2 change ONLY the status-bar clock digits (y1027-1036, x1671-1677); from frame 3 a full-width bar occupies y=970..1039, x=175..1744 (109,872 changed px). The crop is a red SnackBar with both validation messages, fully legible, persisting through its 4 s duration. Case 2 (restore toast): same geometry, green bar reading 'Restored 123 items...'. The stated cause is backwards -- window is 160,150..1760,1050 and the status bar is ~y1019..1050, so the snackbar overlaps it and is painted ON TOP, covering it. Structurally that is expected: app_shell.dart:633-816 makes StatusBar(compact:false) the last child of the shell Scaffold's body Column with no bottomNavigationBar, and Scaffold paints _ScaffoldSlot.snackBar after the body. What produced the original observation is a ~0.5 s gap between click and first painted snackbar frame on the softpipe renderer: any capture inside that window shows nothing while a `tree` read a second later still finds the message. I reproduced that same false negative myself before switching to burst capture -- harness artefact, not defect. Residual real issue worth P3 only: while shown the snackbar hides the status bar, and TransientBottomInset (snackbar_helper.dart:20-27), the mechanism built to prevent exactly that, is published by one screen in the whole app (imaging_screen.dart:153).

findings.title: GLADE+ catalog download is broken end to end: the VizieR TAP endpoint it targets returns 503, and the app's only report of that is a snackbar you cannot see
findings.what_happened: Settings > Catalogs > GLADE+ Galaxy Catalog > 'Download Standard (~50 MB)': the button flips to 'Downloading...' for about 3 seconds, then silently returns to its idle label. glade_plus_galaxies.csv stays 0 bytes and no .partial appears. Only the accessibility tree carries the reason -- 'Download failed: Exception: Annotation catalog download failed' -- and that snackbar is hidden behind the status bar (see the snackbar finding), so on screen the button simply does nothing. The cause is upstream: the URL built by buildGladePlusUrl() targets https://tapvizier.cds.unistra.fr/TAPVizieR/tap/sync, and I reproduced the exact query with curl -- HTTP 503 'No server is available to handle this request' in 0.36 s, while https://vizier.cds.unistra.fr/ itself answers 200. So the one deep-sky catalog the app offers to fetch on demand cannot be fetched at all, on any tier.
findings.expected: A download that cannot succeed should say so in plain language and name the host ('VizieR TAP is not responding (HTTP 503) - try again later, or use Import from File'), and the app should not depend on a single TAP mirror for a 2 GB optional catalog.
findings.repro: Settings > Catalogs > scroll to GLADE+ > Download Standard (~50 MB). Watch: 'Downloading...' -> idle. ls ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/catalogs/glade_plus_galaxies.csv -> still 0 bytes. curl the TAP URL from packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/catalogs/catalog_manager/source_models.dart:337-355 -> 503.
findings.evidence: curl output: code=503 size=108 time=0.36 for the Standard-tier query; tree at t4-t10 after the click: 'Download failed: Exception: Annotation catalog download failed'; file listing showing 0 bytes throughout.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/catalogs/catalog_manager/source_models.dart:337-355 (buildGladePlusUrl) and the download handler in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/catalog_settings_screen.dart
findings.proposed_fix: Surface the HTTP status and host in the error; add a fallback mirror or a pre-built bundle (the app already ships a catalogs-v1 GitHub release for HYG/NGC); keep 'Import from File (CSV)' prominent as the documented workaround.
findings.verdict_reasoning: The download works. I reproduced the exact query buildGladePlusUrl() emits for the Standard tier (source_models.dart:340-356, still targeting tapvizier.cds.unistra.fr/TAPVizieR/tap/sync) with curl: HTTP 200, 4,874,018 bytes of CSV in 9.2 s. Then I drove the UI: Settings > Catalogs > GLADE+ > 'Download Standard (~50 MB)' went to 'Downloading...' with a live 'Downloading: GLADE+ Galaxy Catalog' progress panel, the .partial grew, and it finished with glade_plus_galaxies.csv at 15,635,359 bytes -- no error, no failure snackbar. The 503 the finding measured was a transient VizieR outage, not an app defect, so 'cannot be fetched at all, on any tier' does not hold. Two residuals for a separate ticket: the tier is labelled '~50 MB' but delivers ~15.6 MB, and the download bypasses SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR -- it wrote into the developer's real ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/catalogs/ from a sandboxed instance.

findings.title: The desktop app can never tell you a new version exists: the only 'Updates' page in Settings is for a remote appliance, and the built-in update manager is wired to a server URL nothing ever sets
findings.what_happened: Searching Settings for 'update' returns exactly two entries: About and 'Appliance Updates'. Appliance Updates says 'Connect to a remote appliance to manage its updates. The local desktop app updates itself through its own installer.' and renders nothing else off-network. There is no local update check anywhere in Settings, and About (which the settings catalog even tags with the keyword 'updates') shows only a version string and three web links. The app does ship an in-app updater -- app.dart:204-206 wraps the desktop shell in UpdateManagerWidget, which fires _checkForUpdates() 3 s after launch -- but that check is gated on state.updateServerUrl being non-empty (update_manager_widget.dart:40-43) and the only caller of UpdateNotifier.configure(serverUrl:) in the whole repo is apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/update_wiring.dart, i.e. the appliance server, never the GUI. So on the shipped desktop build the updater is inert: I ran the app for ~40 minutes with working internet and it made no version request, showed no update UI, and logged nothing about updates. The sentence 'updates itself through its own installer' is also not true of the Linux build, which is distributed as a tarball with no installer.
findings.expected: A 'Check for updates' row in About or a Software Update section: current version + build, channel (stable/beta), last checked, and a manual check. NINA and SGP both check at launch and show release notes; an astrophotographer needs to know a fix landed before the night, not after.
findings.repro: Settings > search 'update' -> About, Appliance Updates. Open Appliance Updates on the desktop build: one explanatory sentence, no controls. Open About: version 6.1.0, three links, System Information. No update control anywhere. drive_linux.py log over the whole session contains no update/version request.
findings.evidence: tree of Settings > Appliance Updates (title, subtitle 'Check for, stage, and apply updates to the connected rig', single info panel). Source: packages/skotiq_app/lib/app.dart:204-206, packages/skotiq_updater/lib/src/widgets/update_manager_widget.dart:40-52, packages/skotiq_updater/lib/src/services/update_service.dart:236-239 ('Update server URL not configured'), and grep showing update_wiring.dart:79 as the sole configure() caller.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/update_settings.dart (appliance-only page) and the unconfigured desktop path above
findings.proposed_fix: Configure the update service with the public release feed on desktop startup and give Settings > About a 'Software Update' block (version+build, channel, Check now, last checked). Until that exists, drop the 'updates itself through its own installer' claim.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Live: Settings search 'update' returns exactly About and Appliance Updates. Appliance Updates renders only a title, the subtitle 'Check for, stage, and apply updates to the connected rig' and one info panel 'Connect to a remote appliance to manage its updates. The local desktop app updates itself through its own installer.' -- no controls. About renders version 6.1.0, tagline, three links and System Information; no update control, no build number. Code confirms the dead path at the cited lines: app.dart:204-206 wraps the desktop shell in UpdateManagerWidget; update_manager_widget.dart:39-43 _isUpdateConfigured() and :163-168 _checkForUpdates return early when updateProvider.state.updateServerUrl is empty; the only configure() caller outside the updater package is headless_api/update_wiring.dart:79, reached from desktop_app_bootstrap.dart:377, which builds a SEPARATE UpdateService for the headless API server and needs SKOTIQ_UPDATE_SERVER -- it never touches the Riverpod updateProvider the GUI widget reads.

findings.title: The in-app Logs viewer records nothing about the failures the user just watched happen -- five failed catalog downloads and every rejected save are absent from it and from the 18.8 MB log export
findings.what_happened: Settings > Logs is the surface a user is told to use ('View application logs with filtering and export'). In a session where I triggered the GLADE+ download five times and watched it fail five times, searching the viewer for 'download' gives '0 of 139 entries / No entries match current filters' and searching for 'glade' gives 0 as well. The level filter reports the whole session as one error: Error+ = '1 of 139 entries', the single [ProfileActivationWriteThrough] 'Strict activation aborted: target profile 1 does not exist'. Not logged anywhere: the catalog download failure, the two rejected profile imports, the rejected profile saves, or the two later unhandled 'Cannot activate profile' exceptions that Flutter printed to stderr. I then pressed Export, which produced /home/scdouglas/Documents/skotiq_logs_2026-08-02T11-08-20.txt -- 18,829,614 bytes, 142,921 lines, concatenating the rotated on-disk logs back to 2026-07-27 -- and grepped it: 0 occurrences of 'glade' and 0 of 'annotation catalog download'. The failure genuinely has no persistent record.
findings.expected: Every user-visible failure should leave a log line at WARN/ERROR with the cause (here: the VizieR TAP 503). Otherwise the log viewer gives a user and a support engineer false confidence -- 'only 1 error all night' -- about a session that failed repeatedly.
findings.repro: Settings > Catalogs > Download Standard (~50 MB), which fails. Then Settings > Logs > search 'download' -> 0 of N entries. Set the level filter to Error+ -> 1 of N. Press Export and grep the resulting file for 'glade' -> 0 hits.
findings.evidence: Tree readings '0 of 139 entries / No entries match current filters' for both 'download' and 'glade'; '1 of 139 entries' at Error+ with the single ProfileActivationWriteThrough row; grep -ic glade on the 18.8 MB export -> 0.
findings.where: the catalog download handler in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/catalog_settings_screen.dart (catches and snackbars without logging) and the equivalent swallow in the profile save/import paths
findings.proposed_fix: Log every caught user-facing exception at ERROR with the underlying cause before showing the snackbar.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Confirmed on this session's own failures, with one correction to the specifics. This run produced three user-visible 'Duplicate profile failed: Bad state: ...' snackbars, two rejected profile saves, one unhandled 'Cannot activate profile 6' exception and one successful 15.6 MB GLADE+ download. Settings > Logs then reported: 'duplicat' -> 0 of 124 entries; 'download' -> 0 of 124; 'glade' -> 0 of 124; 'catalog' -> 1; 'profile' -> 2. The only error-level line for the whole session is '[ProfileActivationWriteThrough] Strict activation aborted: target profile 6 does not exist' -- exactly the shape reported. I then pressed Export and grepped the 19,489,798-byte / 147,939-line result: 0 'glade', 0 'duplicat', 0 'annotation catalog'. Mechanism matches the cited location: catalog_settings_screen.dart:1229-1230 catches and calls _showError, which is only context.showErrorSnackBar (:414-418) with no logger call; the duplicate handler does the same at screen_shell.dart:394. Correction: the catalog download SUCCEEDED this time and still produced no log entry, so the gap is 'no catalog-download logging at all, success or failure', not only the failure path.

findings.repro: Settings > search 'replay' > Replay & Debug. Read the header. Press 'Clear all replay history'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-77.png (page), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-82.png (dialog footer: 'Cancel' and 'Clear' identically styled).
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/replay_debug_settings.dart

findings.title: Duplicate reports 'Duplicate profile failed' for a duplicate that succeeded, and leaks an internal invariant message to the user
findings.what_happened: Settings > Equipment Profiles > (profile) > Duplicate > Duplicate, accepting the pre-filled name. The app reported: 'Duplicate profile failed: Bad state: Profile duplication completed, but profile 5 was absent from the refreshed profile list.' The duplicate had in fact succeeded -- equipment_profiles gained row 5 and the profile list in the same screen shows it (three rows: 'Local Work Do Not Lose' [Active], 'Local Work Do Not Lose (Copy)', 'Local Work Do Not Lose (Copy)'). So the message is false in both halves: the operation did not fail, and profile 5 is not absent from the list. It reads like a post-write assertion racing the provider refresh, and the assertion text -- which names a row id and an internal list -- is shown verbatim to the user.
findings.expected: Report success, or if the refresh really has not landed, retry/await it rather than declaring failure. A user who believes this message will press Duplicate again and end up with a third copy.
findings.repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > select a profile > overflow > Duplicate > press Duplicate. (I hit it on the second duplicate of the same source profile, i.e. when the proposed name collided with an existing profile.) sqlite3 <data>/skotiq.db 'select id,name from equipment_profiles' shows the new row; the list in the UI shows it too.
findings.evidence: tree: 'panel: Duplicate profile failed: Bad state: Profile duplication completed, but profile 5 was absent from the refreshed profile list.' alongside DB rows 3,4,5 and a list rendering all three.
findings.where: the duplicate handler in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/equipment_profiles_screen_parts/profile_controls.dart and the profiles notifier's post-duplicate lookup
findings.proposed_fix: Await the refreshed state (or look the row up by id in the DAO result) before asserting; never surface a Bad state message as user copy.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live, 3 times out of 5 duplicates of the same source profile. Duplicates 1 and 2 succeeded silently; 3, 4 and 5 each raised the snackbar 'Duplicate profile failed: Bad state: Profile duplication completed, but profile 4 / 5 / 6 was absent from the refreshed profile list.' while sqlite3 showed rows 4, 5 and 6 present and the list in the same screen rendered all of them (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-31.png). Both halves of the message are false exactly as claimed. It is a post-write refresh race: screen_shell.dart:311-324 _awaitMutatedProfile awaits ref.read(equipmentProfilesProvider.future) after duplicateProfile's ref.invalidateSelf() and throws a StateError when the id is not yet in the returned list; that assertion text goes straight to showErrorSnackBar at :394.
findings.location_wrong: Cited 'the duplicate handler in .../profile_controls.dart'. Both the handler and the message live in .../equipment_profiles_screen_parts/screen_shell.dart -- _duplicateProfile at :362-396, the throw in _awaitMutatedProfile at :311-324, the snackbar at :394. profile_controls.dart holds unrelated widgets (_EditableFilterChip, _DeviceChip).

findings.title: Duplicate happily creates two profiles with byte-identical names, while Import de-duplicates -- so the profile list can show rows nothing can tell apart
findings.what_happened: Duplicating the same profile twice and accepting the offered name both times produced ids 4 and 5, both named 'Local Work Do Not Lose (Copy)'. The list renders two identical rows (same title, same 'No description', same icon) with nothing to distinguish them, and the status-bar profile chip shows only a name, so once one of them is active you cannot tell which. The importer, by contrast, does resolve collisions -- importing a profile named 'Audit Rig Alpha' over an existing one produced 'Audit Rig Alpha (1)'. Two code paths, two different rules.
findings.expected: One rule: reject or auto-suffix a colliding name everywhere. Duplicate should offer '(Copy 2)' the second time, exactly as Import offers '(1)'.
findings.repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > overflow > Duplicate > Duplicate (accept the pre-filled name). Repeat. sqlite3 'select id,name from equipment_profiles' -> two rows with the same name.
findings.evidence: DB: 4|Local Work Do Not Lose (Copy) and 5|Local Work Do Not Lose (Copy); tree shows two identical list rows.
findings.where: the duplicate handler's default name generation vs the importer's collision resolution
findings.proposed_fix: Route both through one uniqueName(base) helper, and add a UNIQUE index on equipment_profiles.name if names are meant to be identifiers.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Duplicating 'Adv Rig One' five times, accepting the pre-filled name each time, produced ids 2,3,4,5,6 all named exactly 'Adv Rig One (Copy)' (sqlite3), rendered as five visually identical rows with the same icon and no subtitle (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-31.png). The offered name is a fixed '${profile.name} (Copy)' built at screen_shell.dart:368 with no collision check, whereas the importer resolves collisions with a '(n)' suffix. P3 is fair -- usability/consistency, not data loss.

findings.title: The 'default startup profile' that Settings > General promises has no UI anywhere -- it is pinned to whichever profile you created first
findings.what_happened: Settings > General > Auto-connect equipment reads 'Connects the default startup profile on launch, falling back to the last active profile when no default is set'. Equipment Profiles has no notion of a default: the badge says 'Active', the header action says 'Set Active', and the overflow menu is Edit / Duplicate / Export / Delete. Nothing shows or sets a default. In the database equipment_profiles.is_default is set on whichever profile was created first and never moves: after I created a profile (is_default=1), duplicated it twice (both is_default=0) and pressed Set Active on a duplicate, the rows read 3|...|is_active=0|is_default=1, 4|...|is_active=1|is_default=0.
